description:
README.md contains code blocks marked ` ```rust ` (not no_run) that no longer
match the public API surface. Two examples won't compile:

1. README.md:65 — verify_chain with 5 arguments:

       let result = verify_chain(&chain, &anchors, &policy, &my_verifier, &NoRevocation)?;

   The current `verify_chain` signature (src/lib.rs:374) is 6 arguments;
   it takes `aia: &A` after `revocation`. The example needs a `&NoAiaFetcher`
   (or other `AiaFetcher`) tail argument. This was introduced by commit
   ec9bb744 / 50e43963 (Verifier 3rd generic for AiaFetcher) and not
   propagated to the README.

2. README.md:35-39, 45-47, 53-56 — CrlChecker::new() / with_delta() / OcspChecker::new()
   are bound directly:

       let checker = CrlChecker::new(crl_der, unix_now(), DefaultVerifier);
       let result = verify_chain_default(&chain, &anchors, &policy, &checker)?;

   `CrlChecker::new` and friends return `Result<Self>` (pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs).
   Binding the Result and then passing `&checker` will not type-check
   — `&Result<CrlChecker>` does not implement `RevocationChecker`. The
   examples need either `.unwrap()`, `?`, or a `let checker = CrlChecker::new(...)?;`.

Both examples are in the README's primary onboarding flow; a new caller
copy-pasting them will hit cargo errors before they learn anything useful.

Suggested fix: add the README as a `#[doc = include_str!(\"../README.md\")]`
in lib.rs (or include the snippets directly) so `cargo test --doc` exercises
them; or convert the README to ```rust,ignore``` blocks. The former is
better — keeps the contract honest.

Caller impact: every new user.
title: README examples for verify_chain and CrlChecker won't compile
